key_insight: A parameter-free, ab initio Green-Kubo framework can predict charge transport in molecular semiconductors by letting full electron–phonon dynamics reveal the dominant transport regime and bottlenecks.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable screening and design of organic electronic materials, including transistors and photovoltaics, by linking atomic structure directly to mobility trends and transport mechanisms.
method: Compute electron–phonon Hamiltonians from first principles without fitting transport parameters.
Propagate carriers over hundreds-of-molecule domains using the full phonon spectrum.
Use nonperturbative Green–Kubo dynamics to extract mobility, temperature dependence, and conductivity fingerprints.
evidence_signal: Across five representative crystals, the method matches measured mobilities, temperature exponents, and optical-conductivity signatures, and it revises the mechanism of DNTT transport.
watch_item: The approach is computationally demanding and may require substantial resources for large-scale or high-throughput materials screening.
paper_title: First-Principles Origins of Charge Transport in Molecular Semiconductors
